questions: If there are ties for the N-th largest absolute difference, should we include all tied differences (making the sample size > N) or break ties arbitrarily to keep exactly N?
Should the t-test be one-tailed or two-tailed? The reference uses stats.ttest_ind default, which is two-tailed, but the prompt doesn't specify.
What should happen if N is greater than the number of rows in the DataFrame? Should we use all rows or raise an error?
Should missing values (NaN) in the specified columns be handled (e.g., dropped, raise error, propagate)?

Does 'largest absolute differences' refer to differences computed as col1 - col2, or col2 - col1? The absolute makes order irrelevant, but sign matters for selecting indices if we take absolute after subtraction.
Should the t-test assume equal variances (default) or not? The clarification mentions it can be overridden but the reference uses default.
If N is exactly 2, the t-test on two samples is possible but may have high p-value; is that acceptable, or should we require a minimum sample size for statistical validity?
Should the function return the p-value as a Python float or a numpy float? The example prints a float, but stats.ttest_ind returns a numpy type.
